record.program_name: Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA) regional program (County, Grass Valley and Nevada City)
record.administering_agency: Nevada County Housing and Community Services Department
record.typical_award_size: $3,074,180 in PLHA for 2020 through 2024 across the County, Grass Valley and Nevada City; Rounds 1 to 3 funded affordable housing development (Lone Oak II and Habitat Ventana Sierra through the trust fund), owner-occupied construction and homeless services; Rounds 4 and 5 total $808,089 and will be awarded directly under the plan amended June 16, 2026 (Resolution 26-317). Per HCD's 2024-2028 formula NOFA the County's own annual allocation is $207,009 (2024) and $238,910 (2025) and Nevada City's is $53,734 and $57,661; Grass Valley's is delegated to the County under the MOU extended August 11, 2026.
record.per_unit_cap: Not published. Rental awards must be low-interest deferred loans secured by a deed of trust with a 55-year regulatory agreement (resolution certification 9).
record.affordability_requirement: PLHA guidelines: households at or below 60% AMI for rental development, with 55-year covenants; owner-occupied units deed-restricted per Guidelines 302(c)(6).
record.next_deadline: No NOFA published as of November 8, 2026. Staff report (August 11, 2026) says the County will score proposals for Rounds 4 and 5 jointly with the two cities once the MOU extension is executed by both city councils.
record.layering_notes: Nevada County's Housing and Community Services Department (HCS, Tyler Barrington, Director, 950 Maidu Ave, Nevada City, 530-265-1645, Housing@nevadacountyca.gov) sits inside the Health and Human Services Agency and administers the Western Nevada County Regional Housing Trust Fund, PLHA (as delegated applicant for Grass Valley and Nevada City), state HOME and CDBG awards, the MORE mobile home program and the new Down Payment Assistance Program; the Behavioral Health and Homelessness Department (Cari Yardley, Director) holds Homekey+, BHSA and the Truckee Navigation Center; HHAP is administered by the Homeless Resource Council of the Sierras as the CoC CA-531 lead; and the Regional Housing Authority (Sutter, Nevada, Yuba, Colusa and Lake counties, Yuba City) supplies vouchers. Grass Valley, Nevada City and Truckee run their own programs (Pass 3). The County has no inclusionary ordinance, no housing impact fee and no affordable housing fee waiver program; the only land use incentive is the state density bonus ordinance. nevadacountyca.gov opens directly and the Legistar web API client 'nevco' exposes staff reports and attachments at legistar.granicus.com/nevco/attachments/. PLHA is small (roughly $200,000 to $300,000 a year countywide) and has historically been bundled into trust fund loans. A developer with a site in the unincorporated area, Grass Valley or Nevada City should contact HCS early to be placed in the Round 4 and 5 pipeline; awards will be 55-year deferred loans suitable as TCAC local contribution. Round 3 money is committed to Lone Oak II and Habitat.

record.program_name: Homeless Housing, Assistance and Prevention (HHAP) via Nevada County Continuum of Care CA-531
record.administering_agency: Homeless Resource Council of the Sierras (CoC CA-531 administrative entity) with Nevada County Health and Human Services Agency
record.typical_award_size: HHAP-6 allocations: Nevada County $588,802.52 and Nevada County CoC $628,851.21; HHAP-7 preliminary: County $594,795.85 and CoC $637,281.27. Total HHAP investment in the Nevada County area since 2019 about $5.4 million. Under the MOU approved September 8, 2026 (Resolution 26-438) the CoC administers Rounds 4, 5, 6 and future rounds and passes 25% of each joint award to the County for homeless operational services and extreme weather shelters.
record.per_unit_cap: Not applicable; no capital set-aside identified.
record.affordability_requirement: People experiencing or at risk of homelessness per the Regionally Coordinated Homeless Action Plan.
record.next_deadline: HHAP-7 applications follow the state 2026 schedule; local funding decisions run through the CoC's Joint Homeless Action Plan process. Contact the Homeless Resource Council of the Sierras.

record.program_name: Conduit tax-exempt bond TEFRA approvals (CMFA, CSCDA) for multifamily rental
record.administering_agency: Nevada County Board of Supervisors (TEFRA hearing) with California Municipal Finance Authority or CSCDA as issuer
record.typical_award_size: April 2026 TEFRA hearing for up to $11,000,000 of CMFA exempt facility bonds for Lone Oak Senior Apartments II, 10528 Broken Oak Court, Penn Valley (borrower Penn Valley Pacific Associates II, developer Pacific West Communities). Amount set by project; County is a CMFA and CSCDA member and holds the Section 147(f) hearing for unincorporated projects.
record.per_unit_cap: Not applicable; sized to 50% test for 4% credits.
record.affordability_requirement: Qualified residential rental project under IRC 142(d) (20% at 50% AMI or 40% at 60% AMI) plus CDLAC and TCAC regulatory agreements.
record.next_deadline: TEFRA hearings are scheduled on request through the Clerk of the Board; allow 30 to 45 days for noticing before the CDLAC application.
